subject: MAP preflight — economic gating + eval sampler (tokens, cache hit, batching SLAs)
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire@nutrisync.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex@nutrisync.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:23:00 -0800
Subject: Quick alignment: prelaunch econ checks before pilot

Hi Dylan —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We want to lock the mutual action plan (MAP) so internal stakeholders can greenlight the pilot. Two asks from our side before procurement moves forward:

1) A concise econ sheet with tokens/$ at expected latency targets (50ms vs 150ms p95) and monthly spend ranges based on 100k–1M requests.
2) Clear assumptions on cache hit-rate (KV/prefix caching) and the batching profile you expect in production — our infra team cares about tail latency tradeoffs.

Can your team share a short doc and an outline of the evaluation plan + gating criteria we can use for internal sign-off? Our procurement lead (cc'd) will need that to scope the SOW.

Best,
Claire
Claire Huang
Head of AI Integrations
NutriSync

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@nutrisync.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, k arthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick alignment: prelaunch econ checks before pilot

Claire —

Thanks, noted. Putting a concise packet together and attaching an initial cost_model_v2.xlsx (tabbed: baseline, 50ms-p95, 150ms-p95, cache-sensitivity). High level calls:

- Tokens/$ assumptions: baseline 0.0008 $/token for the hosted variant; with dedicated reserved capacity we can show effective token costs down to 0.00045 $/token depending on batching and steady-state throughput.
- Key cache assumptions: we listed 3 scenarios — 20%, 45%, 70% prefix/KV cache hit rates. Please review the 'cache-sensitivity' tab.
- Batching profile: recommended per-request batching target is 8–12 tokens/request with 50–120ms batching window for neutral latency. For strict p95 SLAs (<=100ms) we recommend conservative batch targets (<=4) and higher reserved capacity.

I'll propose a short evaluation plan in the next email with explicit gating metrics (units-per-dollar thresholds, latency SLOs, and sample traffic run steps).

Attaching: cost_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Claire Huang <claire@nutrisync.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: k arthik_iyer@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed eval plan + quick sampler run to validate tokens/$

Claire —

Draft eval plan (short):

1) Traffic sampler (3 days): NutriSync will provide production anonymized request samples (100k requests). We will run the sampler on Redwood's hosted environment and dedicated pool. Deliverable: throughput, median/p95 latency, tokens generated per request distribution, observed batch sizes.

2) Cost simulation (2 days): Using the sampler output we will run the cost model with three cache-hit scenarios and two batching profiles. Deliverable: tokens/$ sensitivity table and 3-month spend projection.

3) Gate decision (1 day): NutriSync reviews the tokens/$ and latency curves against acceptance criteria both for pilot and for scale. If tokens/$ for pilot exceeds agreed threshold, we'll iterate quantization/quantized model options.

Acceptance criteria suggestions (examples):
- Pilot tokens/$ <= $0.0007 (hosted) OR <= $0.0005 (dedicated)
- p95 latency <= 150ms for hosted pilot traffic sample
- Cache hit-rate > 40% for the expected prefix set

Timeline we recommend: sampler start Wed 2/18, sampler complete 2/21, cost sim 2/22–2/23, decision 2/24. This aligns with your Q1 procurement window.

I've kicked off a small sampler run with a synthetic 100k trace; early CSV attached (traffic_sampler_results.csv). Initial hit-rate looks ~38% for our default prefix heuristics. Will share updated sims after Claire's real sample.

Thanks —Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Ops — Redwood Inference

Marissa/Dylan —

Thanks for the clear plan and the early sampler output. A couple quick clarifications from our infra and finance teams:

- For the sampling, we can provide sanitized requests (no PII) by EOD Friday. Expect ~120k requests.
- Procurement wants the cost sim run with two additional knobs: a) 10% traffic burst scenario (short spikes) and b) one-month projection with cold-start overheads included.
- Can you add the quantized-ggml variant to the cost model for a sensitivity column (we have a preference toward lower-cost inference if it doesn't degrade correctness beyond a defined eval set).

We are comfortable with the timeline you proposed but need the final MAP (single PDF) to include explicit sign-off lines for Finance/Procurement (I attached a MAP stub in my internal tracker).

Claire

From: k arthik_iyer@redwood.com

Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed eval plan + quick sampler run to validate tokens/$

Claire —

Quick technical notes that we'll include in the MAP PDF before sending to Procurement:

- Cache assumption detail: the 'cache-hit' percentage is measured on the request-output prefix match after prompt normalization. We will provide the normalization rules in an appendix. Cache warm-up behavior: expect 12–24 hours of ramp for a 100k daily traffic profile.
- Batching tradeoffs: experiments show batch sizes >12 increase median throughput by ~18% but add 40–80ms to p95 depending on model and hardware; we will surface a recommended operating point per target p95 SLA.
- Burst handling: with autoscale + burst reserve, short 10–20x bursts are handled but unit-costs rise 30–60% for burst windows — broken out in the 'burst' tab of the spreadsheet.
- Quantized variant: we will add a 'ggml-quant' column; expect ~25–35% savings in tokens/$ equivalent but run longer tails on latency — we'll flag this as a conditional option if NutriSync is OK to trade latency variance for cost.

We'll assemble the MAP PDF (mutual_action_plan_v1.pdf) with the evaluation timeline and explicit procurement sign-off fields and share that by 2/18 morning if your sanitized sample arrives by Friday.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
